meta.title: Ontology-to-action decision architecture
meta.purpose: Make every recommendation traceable through what exists, what was observed, what is justified, what matters, and what action is permitted.
meta.warning: This is a project-authored reasoning method, not an externally validated philosophical theory or professional decision standard.

stages.question: What exists in the domain?
stages.failure: The system cannot tell whether two records refer to the same kind of thing or whether a relationship is meaningful.

stages.question: What was observed or recorded?
stages.failure: A concept is mistaken for evidence, or an unlocated statement is treated as an observation.

stages.question: What does the evidence justify us believing?
stages.failure: The system turns missing data into falsehood, inference into fact, or one source into certainty.

stages.question: What matters, to whom, and with what priority?
stages.failure: The system hides a political, fiduciary, financial or ethical preference inside apparently neutral analysis.

stages.question: What should be done, by whom, under which authority?
stages.failure: The system recommends an unsupported, prohibited, unauthorised or value-incoherent action.

relations.meaning: The record concerns a defined kind of thing.
The observation raises the justification for the claim within a stated scope.
The observation counts against the claim within a stated scope.
The observation narrows or conditions the claim.
The option advances an explicit value or objective.
The option creates a cost or conflict against an explicit value.
The option is not justified unless the required claim reaches its required state.
Law, authority, mandate, capability or risk limits the option.

passes_when: every object has a registered type
jurisdiction and effective time are explicit when material
every observation identifies its source or origin
supporting and contradicting treatments remain visible
required claims satisfy their minimum state
the action is not legally prohibited
the action serves at least one explicit value

invariants: No observation becomes a fact merely because it is stored.
No claim becomes supported without traceable evidence treatment.
No missing fact is silently converted to false.
No recommendation is value-free; its objectives must be named.
No legally prohibited option is rendered as an executable recommendation.
No actor may be assigned an action outside its recorded authority.
Every decision must preserve a why, why-not, and what-would-change-it explanation.
